advances: Conditional symmetry of maximum-entropy triangle rows, followed by likelihood transfer and squared-capacity averaging, gives one absolute actual-depth coefficient for the entire product of arbitrary even-height width-two triangles. Composing this whole group once with the whole accepted simplex-pyramid-box group gives the required intrinsic dyadic second- and third-moment bounds, exact unnormalized third-cap normalization, and saturated affine transport. This enlarges the covered product family; it does not assert coverage of arbitrary supports in the locked problem.
author: research-agent
proof:
We first identify the triangle rows and their normalizations. For each triangle index \(i\) and root \(\mathbf j_i\in A_i\), let \(\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}=r_{A_i,\mathbf j_i}\) be the unique maximum-entropy law with mean \(\mathbf j_i\). Here \(r_{A_i,\mathbf j_i}\) is the entropy row of `bf1ff94487296374`, and \(\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}\) is precisely the row of `191ebba2f13ff6d7` and `af3581e517f3a94e` with height \(M=2m_i\). In those triangle facts, their scalar source parameters \((\tau,\theta)\) equal \((\ell_{i,1},\ell_{i,2})\); their \(\tau\) is not the depth function \(\tau_p\).

Use \(H(\rho):=-\sum_{\rho_{\mathbf x}>0}\rho_{\mathbf x}\log\rho_{\mathbf x}\) and \(D(\rho\|p):=\sum_{\rho_{\mathbf x}>0}\rho_{\mathbf x}\log(\rho_{\mathbf x}/p_{\mathbf x})\), exactly as in `bf1ff94487296374`. Every mean-\(\mathbf j_i\) law \(\rho\) satisfies
\(D(\rho\|p_i)=-H(\rho)-\log p_{i,\mathbf j_i}\), since \(\log p_i\) is affine. Thus relative-entropy minimization and entropy maximization agree, independently of the source tilt. The capacity identity and face assertions in `bf1ff94487296374` give
\[
\mathsf C_{p_i}(\mathbf j_i)
=e^{-D(\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}\|p_i)}
=p_{i,\mathbf j_i}e^{H(\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i})}.
\]
The row is supported on, and positive throughout, the lattice points of the minimal face containing its mean. No ambient attainment of the exponential infimum is required. Also \(\mathsf C_{p_i}(\mathbf j_i)\ge p_{i,\mathbf j_i}>0\), because the root summand has exponential factor one for every normal.

For clarity, all proper triangle faces have exact primitive lattice charts. With \(m=m_i\), the vertical, horizontal, and slanted edges respectively have charts
\[
(x,y)=(0,s),\quad 0\le s\le2m;
\qquad (x,y)=(s,0),\quad 0\le s\le2;
\qquad (x,y)=(0,2m)+s(1,-m),\quad 0\le s\le2.
\]
The parameter \(s\) is integral on the lattice support; the last direction is primitive because its first coordinate is one. The pulled-back source tilts are respectively \(\ell_{i,2}\), \(\ell_{i,1}\), and \(\ell_{i,1}-m\ell_{i,2}\), with the constant \(2m\ell_{i,2}\) on the last edge canceled by conditional normalization. Entropy and mean constraints are preserved by each chart. The face representation in `bf1ff94487296374` therefore makes every nonvertex edge row a geometric interval entropy row with the corresponding integral mean. At the two nonvertical nonvertex roots that scalar mean is one, and the row is uniform on its three edge points: the uniform law is feasible and has maximal entropy by nonnegativity of relative entropy to that uniform law. Vertex rows are Dirac. In particular the case \(m=1\), with no interior lattice root, is included. The accepted cap-mass conclusion of `af3581e517f3a94e` and the variance-price conclusion of `191ebba2f13ff6d7` both include all these face rows.

Define exactly the price variables of `191ebba2f13ff6d7` by
\[
V_{i,\mathbf j_i}:=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}}
 \log\frac{\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}(\mathbf X_i)}{p_i(\mathbf X_i)},
\qquad
\omega_{i,\mathbf j_i}:=
 \frac{p_{i,\mathbf j_i}\mathsf C_{p_i}(\mathbf j_i)^2}{\mathcal B_2(p_i)}.
\]
The logarithm is evaluated only on positive row support. Each \(\omega_i\) is a probability law. By `191ebba2f13ff6d7` and `544d43563ec0b5eb`, respectively, the price and surplus bounds with the preceding aliases are
\[
\mathbb E_{\omega_i}V_{i,\mathbf j_i}\le V_0,
\qquad \mathcal B_2(p_i)\ge g_\triangle/16.
\]
Expanding \(8(110592e^2/9)=98304e^2\) verifies that our displayed \(V_0\) is exactly the admissible choice in the former fact, not a new estimate.

Suppose first \(b\ge1\). Fix a triangle root tuple \(\mathbf j=(\mathbf j_1,\ldots,\mathbf j_b)\), and put \(Q_{\mathbf j}:=\bigotimes_{i=1}^b\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}\). This is the product row of `af3581e517f3a94e`, whose factor-count parameter \(k\) is our \(b\). It is also the maximum-entropy row at \(\mathbf j\) on \(D_\triangle\): for any feasible joint law \(\rho\) with marginals \(\rho_i\),
\[
H(\rho)=\sum_i H(\rho_i)-D\left(\rho\middle\|\bigotimes_i\rho_i\right)
\le\sum_i H(\rho_i)\le\sum_i H(\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i})=H(Q_{\mathbf j}).
\]
Relative entropy is nonnegative by \(\log t\le t-1\); its equality case and uniqueness of each marginal entropy row give uniqueness of this product row.

Capacity factorization is exact, including at face roots:
\[
\mathsf C_{P_\triangle}(\mathbf j)=\prod_{i=1}^b\mathsf C_{p_i}(\mathbf j_i),
\qquad
\mathcal B_2(P_\triangle)=\prod_{i=1}^b\mathcal B_2(p_i).
\]
For the first identity, a product exponential sum equals the product of its block exponential sums. It is at least the product of their positive infima. Conversely, choosing each block normal arbitrarily close to its own infimum gives the reverse inequality. Finite summation with the original root weights proves the second identity. These are the same factorizations as in `bf1ff94487296374`.

The conditional-symmetry conclusion of `af3581e517f3a94e` supplies \(Q_{\mathbf j}(H)\ge\delta_\triangle\) for every containing closed halfspace \(H\). We use that cap conclusion directly; no fourth-moment bound on the original row projections is assumed or deduced.

On the positive support of \(Q_{\mathbf j}\), set
\(L_{\mathbf j}(\mathbf X):=\log(Q_{\mathbf j}(\mathbf X)/P_\triangle(\mathbf X))\) and \(v(\mathbf j):=\sum_i V_{i,\mathbf j_i}\). Independence and the capacity identity give
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_{\mathbf j}}L_{\mathbf j}
=-\log\mathsf C_{P_\triangle}(\mathbf j),
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_{Q_{\mathbf j}}L_{\mathbf j}=v(\mathbf j).
\]
If \(v(\mathbf j)>0\), Chebyshev gives
\[
Q_{\mathbf j}\left(L_{\mathbf j}>
\mathbb E_{Q_{\mathbf j}}L_{\mathbf j}
+\sqrt{\frac{2v(\mathbf j)}{\delta_\triangle}}\right)
\le\frac{\delta_\triangle}{2}.
\]
If \(v(\mathbf j)=0\), then \(L_{\mathbf j}=\mathbb E L_{\mathbf j}\) almost surely, so the same exceptional event with zero threshold is empty. Intersecting the complementary event with \(H\) retains at least \(\alpha_\triangle=\delta_\triangle/2\) of the row mass in either case. On that intersection,
\[
P_\triangle(\mathbf x)=Q_{\mathbf j}(\mathbf x)e^{-L_{\mathbf j}(\mathbf x)}
\ge Q_{\mathbf j}(\mathbf x)\mathsf C_{P_\triangle}(\mathbf j)
 \exp\left(-\sqrt{\frac{2v(\mathbf j)}{\delta_\triangle}}\right).
\]
Summing there and taking the halfspace infimum proves the pointwise actual-depth bound
\[
\tau_{P_\triangle}(\mathbf j)
\ge\alpha_\triangle\mathsf C_{P_\triangle}(\mathbf j)
 \exp\left(-\sqrt{\frac{2v(\mathbf j)}{\delta_\triangle}}\right).
\]
Only nonnegative source mass outside the retained row event is omitted.

Square this bound and average under the unchanged original root law \(P_\triangle\). With \(\Omega:=\bigotimes_{i=1}^b\omega_i\), exact factorization gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal M_2(P_\triangle)
&\ge\alpha_\triangle^2\mathcal B_2(P_\triangle)
 \mathbb E_\Omega\exp\left(-2\sqrt{\frac{2v(\mathbf j)}{\delta_\triangle}}\right),\\
\mathbb E_\Omega v(\mathbf j)
&=\sum_i\mathbb E_{\omega_i}V_{i,\mathbf j_i}\le bV_0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The law \(\Omega\) is only an algebraic reweighting of the squared-capacity sum. Neither the source probabilities in cap masses nor the original root weights defining \(\mathcal M_2\) have been replaced.

For every \(\gamma>0\), the function \(t\mapsto e^{-\gamma\sqrt t}\) is convex and decreasing on \([0,\infty)\). Indeed, concavity of the square root gives
\(e^{-\gamma\sqrt{\lambda s+(1-\lambda)t}}\le e^{-\gamma(\lambda\sqrt s+(1-\lambda)\sqrt t)}\le\lambda e^{-\gamma\sqrt s}+(1-\lambda)e^{-\gamma\sqrt t}\) for \(0\le\lambda\le1\), using convexity of the exponential for the second inequality. This also proves convexity at zero. Jensen, monotonicity, and the price bound therefore give
\[
\mathbb E_\Omega\exp\left(-2\sqrt{\frac{2v(\mathbf j)}{\delta_\triangle}}\right)
\ge\exp\left(-2\sqrt{\frac{2\mathbb E_\Omega v(\mathbf j)}{\delta_\triangle}}\right)
\ge e^{-2\beta_\triangle\sqrt b}.
\]
Together with the gain in `544d43563ec0b5eb`, this proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal M_2(P_\triangle)
&\ge\alpha_\triangle^2
 \exp\left(b\log g_\triangle-2\beta_\triangle\sqrt b\right)4^{-2b},\\
b\log g_\triangle-2\beta_\triangle\sqrt b
&=\log g_\triangle\left(\sqrt b-\frac{\beta_\triangle}{\log g_\triangle}\right)^2
 -\frac{\beta_\triangle^2}{\log g_\triangle}
\ge-\frac{\beta_\triangle^2}{\log g_\triangle}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Completing the square once for the whole group yields \(\mathcal M_2(P_\triangle)\ge a_\triangle^2 4^{-2b}\). If \(b=0\), this group is a singleton with moment exactly one, so the same bound holds because \(a_\triangle<1\). The constants satisfy \(0<a_\triangle<\alpha_\triangle<1\).

For any original finite root law \(p\), Jensen for \(t\mapsto t^{3/2}\) gives \(\mathcal M_3(p)=\mathbb E_p[(\tau_p^2)^{3/2}]\ge\mathcal M_2(p)^{3/2}\). Applying this to \(P_\triangle\) proves its third-moment bound, including the empty group.

By `f1b85039a5de43a6`, applied with the exact support, tilt, rank, and coefficient aliases in the statement, the entire other group satisfies \(\mathcal M_2(P_{\mathrm{mix}})\ge a_{\mathrm{mix}}^2 4^{-R_{\mathrm{mix}}}\). This includes all independently varying simplex and pyramid ranks, all simplex dilations, all interval lengths, all singleton factors, all finite source tilts, and the empty group.

Actual depth is supermultiplicative, with the same normalization as in `bf1ff94487296374`. To verify this directly, fix two finite laws \(p,q\), a product root \((\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\), and a containing halfspace. Its parallel translate through that root has event
\(\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf X-\mathbf x)+\mathbf w\cdot(\mathbf Y-\mathbf y)\ge0\). This event contains the product of the two centered block-cap events where the separate summands are nonnegative. Each event has probability at least the corresponding actual depth; a zero block normal has probability one. Independence and then the halfspace infimum give \(\tau_{p\otimes q}(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\ge\tau_p(\mathbf x)\tau_q(\mathbf y)\). Squaring and summing with the original product root weights yields \(\mathcal M_2(p\otimes q)\ge\mathcal M_2(p)\mathcal M_2(q)\). The singleton conventions make this valid for an empty group too.

Apply this once to \(P_\triangle\) and \(P_{\mathrm{mix}}\). Then
\[
\mathcal M_2(P)\ge a_\triangle^2a_{\mathrm{mix}}^2
 4^{-2b-R_{\mathrm{mix}}}=a^2 4^{-R},
\qquad
\mathcal M_3(P)\ge\mathcal M_2(P)^{3/2}\ge a^3 8^{-R}.
\]
Thus neither coefficient is multiplied once per factor. The stated root-moment inequalities follow by taking roots, and \(0<a<1\) follows from \(0<a_{\mathrm{mix}}<1\).

We now verify actual-cap normalization and the affine assertions. In positive ambient dimension, any halfspace \(\{\mathbf x:\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf x\ge t\}\) containing \(\mathbf j\) has \(t\le\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf j\), and contains its centered cap through \(\mathbf j\). Conversely each nonzero-normal centered cap is such a halfspace. The zero normal gives full support, a trace realizable by a proper halfspace on any finite support in positive ambient dimension, and cannot decrease the infimum. This proves that our centered definition is actual closed-halfspace depth. On a dimension-zero singleton the only containing trace is full, giving the stated convention. A coordinate-block permutation just pulls back normals by the inverse permutation, so product ordering does not affect any quantity.

The exponential weights factorize, giving exactly \(T=b_{\mathrm{cap}}\prod_iZ_i\) and \(c/T=P\). Every actual unnormalized cap mass is \(T\) times its normalized mass, hence \(h_c(\mathbf j)=T\tau_P(\mathbf j)\). There is one further factor of \(T\) from the original unnormalized root weight, so
\[
\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{cap}}(c)
=\sum_{\mathbf j}T P_{\mathbf j}(T\tau_P(\mathbf j))^3
=T^4\mathcal M_3(P)\ge T^4a^3 8^{-R}.
\]
This verifies the exact fourth power, with no capacity substituted for actual depth.

Each triangle is complete in its coordinate lattice by its defining inequalities \(x\ge0,y\ge0,m_i x+y\le2m_i\), and contains \(\mathbf0,(1,0),(0,1)\). For the nontriangle group, `f1b85039a5de43a6` supplies completeness after deleting its constant coordinates and both intrinsic ranks. One can also check its factors directly: the simplex inequalities define exactly its stated integer points; for the pyramid, the convex hull has \(0\le t\le2\) and \(|x_h|\le1-t/2\), so at integer heights \(t=0,1,2\) its integer points are exactly the stated support. At \(t=1\) all \(x_h\) are zero. Intervals and singletons are complete as well. Each retained factor contains zero and every corresponding coordinate unit vector. The convex hull of a Cartesian product is the product of the convex hulls: to prove the nontrivial inclusion, multiply the block convex-combination coefficients to obtain a convex combination of product points. Therefore
\(D_{\mathrm{red}}=\operatorname{conv}(D_{\mathrm{red}})\cap\mathbb Z^R\), and \(D_{\mathrm{red}}\) contains \(\mathbf0\) and all standard unit vectors. Its affine hull is \(\mathbb R^R\) and its difference lattice is \(\mathbb Z^R\). Inserting the removed zero coordinates proves both rank assertions for \(D\), including \(R=0\).

The chart \(\psi\) preserves individual weights and original probabilities, since removed coordinates are deterministic zero and their partition-function factors are one. Deleting or inserting zero normal components identifies all affine inequality traces, and hence depths. It also identifies the exponential infima. Its intrinsic weights are exactly \(b_{\mathrm{cap}}e^{\boldsymbol\ell_{\mathrm{red}}\cdot\mathbf y}\).

For \(\Phi\), injectivity and the zero and unit-vector points give
\(\operatorname{aff}(A')=\mathbf v+B\mathbb R^R\) and \(\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}(A'-A')=B\mathbb Z^R\). Saturation and \(\mathbf v\in\mathbb Z^n\) give \(\operatorname{aff}(A')\cap\mathbb Z^n=\mathbf v+B\mathbb Z^R\). If \(\mathbf z\in\operatorname{conv}(A')\cap\mathbb Z^n\), it has representations \(\mathbf z=\mathbf v+B\mathbf y=\mathbf v+B\mathbf h\) with \(\mathbf y\in\operatorname{conv}(D_{\mathrm{red}})\) and \(\mathbf h\in\mathbb Z^R\). Injectivity forces \(\mathbf y=\mathbf h\), and intrinsic completeness forces \(\mathbf y\in D_{\mathrm{red}}\). This proves \(A'=\operatorname{conv}(A')\cap\mathbb Z^n\) and the asserted intrinsic ranks.

An ambient affine inequality \(\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf z\ge t\) pulls back to
\((B^{\mathsf T}\mathbf u)\cdot\mathbf y\ge t-\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v\). Column rank makes \(B^{\mathsf T}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^R\) surjective, so every nonconstant intrinsic inequality also extends to an ambient one. Constant inequalities give full or empty traces, realized by proper halfspaces on a finite support in positive ambient dimension. In dimension zero these are the constant-inequality trace convention, and the only containing trace is full. Thus all containing closed-cap traces correspond in both directions. Pushing individual weights and probabilities forward unchanged preserves their total \(T\), cap masses, original root weights, actual depths, and moments. There is no determinant or lattice-index factor.

Capacity transport follows from the same surjectivity:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf C_{P'}(\Phi(\mathbf j))
&=\inf_{\mathbf u\in\mathbb R^n}
 \sum_{\mathbf y\in D_{\mathrm{red}}}P_{\psi(\mathbf y)}
 e^{(B^{\mathsf T}\mathbf u)\cdot(\mathbf y-\mathbf j)}\\
&=\inf_{\mathbf w\in\mathbb R^R}
 \sum_{\mathbf y\in D_{\mathrm{red}}}P_{\psi(\mathbf y)}
 e^{\mathbf w\cdot(\mathbf y-\mathbf j)}
=\mathsf C_P(\psi(\mathbf j)).
\end{aligned}
\]
This also preserves \(\mathcal B_2\). Mean constraints and entropy are preserved by an injective affine chart and its inverse on the affine hull, so maximum-entropy rows push forward to the corresponding maximum-entropy rows, including proper-face rows. Relative likelihoods on their positive supports are unchanged. The transport of depths and capacities needs only real injectivity; integrality and saturation justify the ambient lattice-completeness assertion.

Surjectivity supplies a solution of \(B^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\ell'=\boldsymbol\ell_{\mathrm{red}}\). With \(b'=b_{\mathrm{cap}}e^{-\boldsymbol\ell'\cdot\mathbf v}\), direct substitution gives
\[
b'e^{\boldsymbol\ell'\cdot\Phi(\mathbf y)}
=b_{\mathrm{cap}}e^{-\boldsymbol\ell'\cdot\mathbf v}
 e^{\boldsymbol\ell'\cdot(\mathbf v+B\mathbf y)}
=b_{\mathrm{cap}}e^{\boldsymbol\ell_{\mathrm{red}}\cdot\mathbf y}
=c_{\psi(\mathbf y)}.
\]
Conversely any ambient weights \(b'e^{\boldsymbol\ell'\cdot\mathbf z}\) pull back to prefactor \(b'e^{\boldsymbol\ell'\cdot\mathbf v}\) and tilt \(B^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\ell'\). This tilt splits into arbitrary permitted block tilts; any removed zero-coordinate tilts can be set to zero without affecting probabilities. Thus every finite ambient tilt on the image is covered with original probabilities unchanged. Since \(n\ge R\), the intrinsic bounds imply the claimed weaker ambient bounds. If \(R=0\), every factor is a singleton or both groups are empty; there is exactly one support point, whose depth and capacity are one and whose unnormalized third moment is \(T^4\). This concludes all cases.
statement:
All logarithms are natural. The convex body \(C\) and mixed set \(S\) of the locked problem retain their meanings. The finite supports below are denoted by \(A_i,D,D_{\mathrm{red}},A'\), and \(\mathsf C_p\) denotes exponential capacity, not the convex body \(C\).

Choose any integer \(b\ge0\), arbitrary integers \(m_i\ge1\) for \(1\le i\le b\), and put
\[
A_i:=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(0,2m_i),(2,0)\}\cap\mathbb Z^2
=\{(0,y):0\le y\le2m_i\}\cup\{(1,y):0\le y\le m_i\}\cup\{(2,0)\}.
\]
Each \(A_i\) is exactly the support denoted \(D_M\) in accepted facts `191ebba2f13ff6d7`, `544d43563ec0b5eb`, and `af3581e517f3a94e`, with their height \(M=2m_i\). Its rank is \(r_i=2\) and its displayed dimension is \(n_i=2\).

Choose also an arbitrary finite index set \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{mix}}\), possibly empty, disjoint from \(\{1,\ldots,b\}\). For each \(i\in\mathcal J_{\mathrm{mix}}\), choose one of the following supports:

- A standard lattice simplex \(A_i=D_{m_i,r_i}:=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{r_i}:\sum_{h=1}^{r_i}x_h\le m_i\}\), with integers \(m_i,r_i\ge1\) and \(n_i=r_i\).
- A width-two cube pyramid \(A_i:=(\{0\}\times\{-1,0,1\}^{k_i})\cup\{(1,\mathbf0),(2,\mathbf0)\}\), with integer \(k_i\ge1\) and \(n_i=r_i=k_i+1\).
- An interval \(A_i=I_{L_i}:=\{0,\ldots,L_i-1\}\), with integer \(L_i\ge1\), \(n_i=1\), and \(r_i=\mathbf1_{\{L_i\ge2\}}\).
- A singleton \(A_i=\{\mathbf0_{n_i}\}\), with integer \(n_i\ge0\) and \(r_i=0\).

A rank-zero simplex is included as a singleton, and the degenerate pyramid \(\{0,1,2\}\) is included as \(I_3\). These are precisely the supports of accepted fact `f1b85039a5de43a6`; the pyramid above is its \(D_{k_i}\), without identifying that legacy symbol with the triangle notation \(D_M\). Its absolute coefficient \(a\in(0,1)\) is denoted by \(a_{\mathrm{mix}}\), with no rescaling.

Write \(\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,b\}\cup\mathcal J_{\mathrm{mix}}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{mix}}:=\sum_{i\in\mathcal J_{\mathrm{mix}}}r_i\). For arbitrary finite real tilts \(\boldsymbol\ell_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\), define the original source laws and their products by
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_{i,\mathbf x}&:=\frac{e^{\boldsymbol\ell_i\cdot\mathbf x}}{Z_i},
&Z_i&:=\sum_{\mathbf y\in A_i}e^{\boldsymbol\ell_i\cdot\mathbf y},
&P&:=\bigotimes_{i\in\mathcal J}p_i,\\
D&:=\prod_{i\in\mathcal J}A_i\subseteq\mathbb Z^{n_0},
&n_0&:=\sum_{i\in\mathcal J}n_i,
&R&:=\sum_{i\in\mathcal J}r_i=2b+R_{\mathrm{mix}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(D_\triangle=\prod_{i=1}^b A_i\), \(P_\triangle=\bigotimes_{i=1}^b p_i\), and \(P_{\mathrm{mix}}:=\bigotimes_{i\in\mathcal J_{\mathrm{mix}}}p_i\). In applying `f1b85039a5de43a6` to the nontriangle group, its index set is \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{mix}}\), its support \(D\) is \(\prod_{i\in\mathcal J_{\mathrm{mix}}}A_i\), its law \(P\) is \(P_{\mathrm{mix}}\), and its rank \(R\) is \(R_{\mathrm{mix}}\). Every empty product is the probability-one point in dimension zero. Products can be presented in any coordinate-block order.

For any probability law \(p\) on a nonempty finite support \(A\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), use
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_p(\mathbf j)&:=\inf_{\mathbf u\in\mathbb R^n}
 \sum_{\substack{\mathbf x\in A\\\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf x-\mathbf j)\ge0}}p_{\mathbf x},
&\mathcal M_q(p)&:=\sum_{\mathbf j\in A}p_{\mathbf j}\tau_p(\mathbf j)^q\quad(q=2,3),\\
\mathsf C_p(\mathbf j)&:=\inf_{\mathbf u\in\mathbb R^n}
 \sum_{\mathbf x\in A}p_{\mathbf x}e^{\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf x-\mathbf j)},
&\mathcal B_2(p)&:=\sum_{\mathbf j\in A}p_{\mathbf j}\mathsf C_p(\mathbf j)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\tau_p\) is actual closed-halfspace depth. In positive ambient dimension it agrees with the infimum over all containing closed halfspaces; on a singleton, including dimension zero, depth and normalized capacity are one. In dimension zero, closed cap traces mean affine-inequality traces, whose only containing trace is full. The quantities \(\tau_p,\mathsf C_p,\mathcal B_2,\mathcal M_2\) have exactly the normalizations of `bf1ff94487296374`, whose ambient dimension variable is the present \(n\), and all displayed moments have the normalizations of `f1b85039a5de43a6`. All root weights in \(\mathcal M_q\) are the original probabilities.

Use the following absolute constants. The constant \(\delta_\triangle\) is exactly that of `af3581e517f3a94e`; \(g_\triangle\) is the constant \(g\) of `544d43563ec0b5eb`; and the displayed \(V_0\) equals the admissible variance constant in `191ebba2f13ff6d7` after expanding its auxiliary constants:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\delta_\triangle&:=\frac1{8\max\{20288,144e^8,2982528\}},
&g_\triangle&:=1+\frac1{16000000},\\
V_0&:=2\left(4+\frac{32}{e^2}\right)
 +98304e^2\left(2\left[\log(18e^2\sqrt{384})+\frac12\log(16e^2)+2\right]^2+\frac{288}{e^2}\right)+1120e^2,\\
\alpha_\triangle&:=\frac{\delta_\triangle}{2},
&\beta_\triangle&:=\sqrt{\frac{2V_0}{\delta_\triangle}},\\
a_\triangle&:=\alpha_\triangle\exp\left(-\frac{\beta_\triangle^2}{2\log g_\triangle}\right),
&a&:=a_\triangle a_{\mathrm{mix}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The symbols \(\alpha_\triangle,\beta_\triangle\) are conversion constants, not row column probabilities or row tilts. Both \(a_\triangle\) and \(a\) lie in \((0,1)\), independently of all heights, ranks, factor counts, and source tilts. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal M_2(P_\triangle)&\ge a_\triangle^2\,4^{-2b},
&\mathcal M_3(P_\triangle)&\ge\mathcal M_2(P_\triangle)^{3/2}\ge a_\triangle^3\,8^{-2b},\\
\mathcal M_2(P)&\ge a^2\,4^{-R},
&\mathcal M_3(P)&\ge\mathcal M_2(P)^{3/2}\ge a^3\,8^{-R}.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular \(\mathcal M_2(P)^{1/2}\ge a2^{-R}\) and \(\mathcal M_3(P)^{1/3}\ge a2^{-R}\). The coefficient \(a_\triangle\) is charged once for the entire triangle group and \(a_{\mathrm{mix}}\) once for the entire other group.

For \(\boldsymbol\ell=(\boldsymbol\ell_i)_{i\in\mathcal J}\) and arbitrary \(b_{\mathrm{cap}}>0\), give \(D\) weights \(c_{\mathbf x}=b_{\mathrm{cap}}e^{\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf x}\). Put \(T:=\sum_{\mathbf x\in D}c_{\mathbf x}=b_{\mathrm{cap}}\prod_i Z_i\), so \(c/T=P\). Define actual unnormalized cap depth by \(h_c(\mathbf j):=\inf_{H\ni\mathbf j}\sum_{\mathbf x\in D\cap H}c_{\mathbf x}\), where \(H\) ranges over closed halfspaces, and set \(h_c=T\) on a singleton. Then
\[
\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{cap}}(c):=\sum_{\mathbf j\in D}c_{\mathbf j}h_c(\mathbf j)^3
=T^4\mathcal M_3(P)\ge T^4a^3\,8^{-R}.
\]
This is the actual-cap normalization of `f1b85039a5de43a6`, not a third moment of exponential capacities.

The intrinsic affine and difference-lattice ranks of \(D\) are both \(R\). Delete its constant zero coordinates to obtain \(D_{\mathrm{red}}\subseteq\mathbb Z^R\), and let \(\psi:\mathbb R^R\to\mathbb R^{n_0}\) insert those zero coordinates. Write \(\boldsymbol\ell_{\mathrm{red}}\) for the retained tilt coordinates. For every integer \(n\ge R\), integral translation \(\mathbf v\in\mathbb Z^n\), and matrix \(B\in\mathbb Z^{n\times R}\) of column rank \(R\) satisfying
\(B\mathbb Z^R=(B\mathbb R^R)\cap\mathbb Z^n\), define \(\Phi(\mathbf y)=\mathbf v+B\mathbf y\) and \(A'=\Phi(D_{\mathrm{red}})\). Then \(A'=\operatorname{conv}(A')\cap\mathbb Z^n\), and both intrinsic ranks of \(A'\) are \(R\).

Under \(c'_{\Phi(\mathbf y)}=c_{\psi(\mathbf y)}\) and \(P'_{\Phi(\mathbf y)}=P_{\psi(\mathbf y)}\), all closed cap traces, individual original probabilities, trace masses, actual depths, normalized exponential capacities, and the displayed moments are preserved. The exact parameter map is
\[
B^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\ell'=\boldsymbol\ell_{\mathrm{red}},
\qquad b'=b_{\mathrm{cap}}e^{-\boldsymbol\ell'\cdot\mathbf v},
\qquad c'_{\mathbf z}=b'e^{\boldsymbol\ell'\cdot\mathbf z}\quad(\mathbf z\in A').
\]
A solution \(\boldsymbol\ell'\in\mathbb R^n\) always exists. Conversely, arbitrary finite ambient tilts \(\boldsymbol\ell'\) and positive prefactors \(b'\) on this image pull back to tilt \(B^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\ell'\) and prefactor \(b'e^{\boldsymbol\ell'\cdot\mathbf v}\), so every such ambient log-affine law is covered. Thus the same bounds hold on \(A'\), and imply the weaker bounds with \(4^{-n},8^{-n},T^4 8^{-n}\). When \(R=0\), all normalized depths, capacities, and moments are exactly one, and \(\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{cap}}(c)=T^4\).
